# PR #3307: Patch: a job ran over 7 minutes

Closes #3305

## What changed

`rust (test server practice rulings)` now runs its test step in about 5 s locally instead of 154 s. I only edited `crates/server/tests/api/practice.rs`.

The cost was in `honest_win()`, which plays seeds in batches of `available_parallelism()` and joins the whole batch. The selected game, the lowest winning seed, finished in about 3 s. The batch then waited about 150 s for a slower game that nothing selects.

- **`play_unless`:** `play` becomes `play_unless(seed, setup, human, abandoned)`. It asks `abandoned()` before each action and returns `None` if the game is given up. `play` stays as a thin wrapper that never abandons, so its ~40 call sites are untouched.
- **`honest_win`:** each batch shares an `AtomicUsize` holding the lowest place that has won so far. A game stops when a lower place of its batch has already won.
- **Same selected game:** a game at or below the final lowest winner is never stopped, so it always runs to its end. `find_map` over the batch picks the lowest place, as the old `find` did.
- **New test:** `a_game_the_search_gives_up_on_stops_before_its_next_action` checks that `play_unless` returns `None` when told to stop. It also checks that `abandoned` is asked exactly 4 times with a limit of 3, once before each action and not again after it says yes.

## Why no shard count was raised

The cost was one game that nothing selects. A count would make every shard holding an `honest_win` user pay the same 150 s plus a full compile. A count change would also turn `bot selftest` red, because `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` pins the committed counts and the bot may not edit `bot/`. A pull request that changes only `scripts/ci-shards.toml` skips that job, so `main` would go red later. `scripts/ci-shards.toml` is unchanged, and nothing under `.github/`, `bot/`, `.harness/` or `.squishy/` is touched.

## How I tested

Local 4-core box, with the engine and cards at Cargo.toml's opt-level 2 as the practice groups build them:

- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. I did not run the workspace clippy or the full workspace tests, since the harness runs them after this.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server -- api::practice::r`: `27 passed; 0 failed; … finished in 5.32s` (before: 154 s).
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server -- api::practice:: --skip api::practice::r`: `19 passed; 0 failed; … finished in 5.02s`.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server -- a_game_the_search_gives_up_on`: `1 passed`.
- `taskset -c 0 cargo test … an_honest_win_pays_practice_rates` (batch size 1): passed in 3.19 s.
- `cargo jackioh spec check`: `1774 rulings, 4388 proofs, 54275 citations in 3502 files, 23424 links: ok`.

## Decisions

- **Plan followed:** I followed the plan's code as written. Clippy's `type_complexity` did not fire, so I added no `Played` alias and no `#[allow]`.
- **No ruling:** none is added or cited, because this is test-support code. I wrote no `R<n>` token in the new comments.
- **Ordering:** I used `Ordering::Relaxed`. `fetch_min` only lowers the value, so a stale read only stops a game later, never wrongly.
- **Test registration:** the new test calls `jackioh_cards::register_all()` itself, because `play_unless` needs the catalog and a plain `#[test]` does not go through the app setup. The test name starts with `a`, so it runs in the `server practice` group, not the rulings one.

## Look twice

- **Headroom is thin.** I can't measure CI's runner. The fixed part of the job is checkout, cache restore and an opt-level 2 compile, and a count can't cut it. My estimate is about 4m 30s to 4m 40s. If `ci duration` still lists this job, a person could try the optional opt-level change the plan names: append `--config profile.test.package.jackioh-engine.opt-level=1 --config profile.test.package.jackioh-cards.opt-level=1` before ` -- ` in the `test` of `server practice` and `server practice rulings` in `.github/ci/rust-test.toml`. I did not measure it.
- **Stale comment:** the comment above those groups ("each claim has the server re-run a whole practice game's AI") no longer holds, since the claim no longer runs the AI. A person could refresh it in the same `.github/` edit.
- **Latent trap, for a person:** any future count change in `scripts/ci-shards.toml` needs a person to update `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` in the same change. Its `JOBS` list and its `{(shard, shards)} == {(1, 1)}` assertion pin the counts.

### Its own review

Built and checked on `claude-4`. This is a draft while its own review run, on the same subscription, reviews it adversarially and fixes what it finds (up to 3 rounds); CI runs on it meanwhile. Once that review approves it, it is marked ready and auto-merge turns on.

| Round | Builder | Checks | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | build, 17.6 min | green | - |

| Gate | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|
| rustfmt (`cargo fmt --check`) | pass | 6s |
| catalog (`cargo jackioh catalog check`) | pass | 0s |
| patches (`cargo jackioh patches check`) | pass | 1s |
| rulings (`cargo jackioh spec check`) | pass | 2s |
| clippy (`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`) | pass | 141s |
| cargo tests (`cargo test --workspace --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts && test -z "$(git status --porcelain -- apps/web/src/wire)"`) | pass | 1334s |
| web tests (`sh scripts/build-wasm.sh && pnpm exec vitest run --project web --changed origin/main --exclude '**/src/audio/**' --exclude '**/src/fx/**' --exclude '**/src/cards/art/convention.test.ts'`) | pass | 182s |

# #3305: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[CI run 42212745234](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42212745234) on `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-3297-4e4163132ee942abd4dba700b1bf1e1ea50da0c0` (`0512302`, merge_group) had jobs over the 7-minute alert (#73):

| Job | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [rust (test server practice rulings)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42212745234/job/127877841081) | 7m 1s | success |

Split the slow job further until every job finishes under the 5-minute target, not just under the 7-minute alert, so the fix has headroom. Most splits are a count in `scripts/ci-shards.toml` (#3072): `web (unit k/K)`, `e2e smoke (k/K)` (for e2e, also refresh the `WEIGHTS` in `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`), or a `rust (test <group>)` group, whose count runs its tests in that many jobs, split by name. A count splits the run, not the compile: a group slow to compile needs its tests in more binaries (the engine's `rules_<n>` each get a job by themselves). Anything that cannot be made fast belongs in the daily `.github/workflows/super.yml`, not in CI.

Night bot: you cannot change `.github/`, and a count or a new `rules_<n>` needs no change there. When the split needs a new group or other flags in `.github/ci/rust-test.toml`, or any other change under `.github/`, make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-4` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42222098064)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`rust (test server practice rulings)` must finish well under 5 minutes, down from 7m 1s. A shard count cannot do this, and measurement shows why:

- I built the server test binary locally on 4 cores, with the engine and cards at opt-level 2 as in CI.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server -- api::practice::r` runs 27 tests in **154 s**.
- 152 s of that is `honest_win()` in `crates/server/tests/api/practice.rs`. Three tests of this group call it: `r1304001_…`, `r1303003_a_paid_game_…` and `r1688000_a_pay_the_store_fails_once_…`.
- With those three skipped, the other 24 tests run in 1.4 s. One `honest_win` user alone takes 153 s.
- `honest_win` plays seeds in batches of `available_parallelism()` and joins the whole batch. A thread trace shows only one game thread still busy from about 8 s to 150 s, and that one is never the selected game.
- Run under `taskset -c 0`, the games are played one at a time and the same test takes **3.4 s**. The first win is quick; only the join waits.
- A count K only helps if tests are spread out. Here every shard that holds one of the three `honest_win` users pays the same 150 s plus a full compile.
- A count would also turn `bot selftest` red. `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` pins the committed counts (its `JOBS` list and `{(shard, shards)} == {(1, 1)}`), and the bot may not edit `bot/`. #3263 did this and #3280 had to repair it. A pull request that changes only `scripts/ci-shards.toml` skips `bot selftest`, so main would go red later.

So the fix is to stop the games that cannot be selected. The selected game stays the lowest-seed win, so no test sees a different game. The sibling group `server practice` calls `honest_win` in three tests too, so it speeds up as well.

## Files to touch

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `crates/server/tests/api/practice.rs` | change: `play` becomes `play_unless` plus a thin `play` wrapper. `honest_win` abandons games that can no longer be the first win. One new test. |

Do not touch these:
- `scripts/ci-shards.toml`: keep every count as it is.
- `bot/`, `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`.
- Any other crate, `spec/`, `CLAUDE.md`.

No ruling is added or cited. This is test-support code, and Hearthstone semantics are not involved. Do not write any `R<n>` token in the new comments.

## Steps

1. In `crates/server/tests/api/practice.rs`, turn `fn play` (about line 240) into `play_unless`. Keep its doc comment and body, and change only these places:
   - New signature (drop-in, keep the existing `///` lines above it and add a final sentence: "`abandoned` is asked before each action: a game it gives up on is `None`."):
     ```rust
     fn play_unless(
         seed: &str,
         setup: &PracticeSetup,
         human: Human,
         abandoned: &dyn Fn() -> bool,
     ) -> Option<(Vec<Action>, ClaimedResult, GameState)> {
     ```
   - First statement inside `while state.result.is_none() {`, before the existing `assert!(log.len() < MOVE_CAP, …)`:
     ```rust
     if abandoned() {
         return None;
     }
     ```
   - The last line `(log, claimed, state)` becomes `Some((log, claimed, state))`.
2. Immediately after `play_unless`'s closing brace, add the wrapper. All ~40 existing `play(...)` call sites stay untouched:
   ```rust
   /// `play_unless` for a game nobody gives up on.
   fn play(seed: &str, setup: &PracticeSetup, human: Human) -> (Vec<Action>, ClaimedResult, GameState) {
       play_unless(seed, setup, human, &|| false).expect("a game nobody abandons ends")
   }
   ```
3. Replace the doc comment and body of `honest_win` (about lines 290–321). Keep `type Won`, the `OnceLock`, the `setup`, `seeds` and `cores` lines, and the final `panic!` exactly as they are. Only the doc comment and the `for batch …` loop change. This is the code to use; if it does not compile, fix borrows and types only, not the logic:
   ```rust
   /// First won Easy game: the lowest seed whose game the human wins, played across cores in
   /// parallel to avoid test timeouts (#2223). A game stops as soon as a lower seed of its batch has
   /// won, since it can no longer be the first: a batch used to wait for its slowest game (about
   /// 150 s) after the first seed had won in 3 s (#3305).
   fn honest_win() -> &'static Won {
       static WON: OnceLock<Won> = OnceLock::new();
       WON.get_or_init(|| {
           let setup = setup(Difficulty::Easy, Vec::new());
           let seeds: Vec<String> = (0..WIN_SEEDS).map(|n| format!("practice-win-{n}")).collect();
           let cores = std::thread::available_parallelism().map_or(1, |cores| cores.get());
           for batch in seeds.chunks(cores) {
               // The place in this batch of the lowest seed that has won so far.
               let lowest_win = AtomicUsize::new(usize::MAX);
               let played: Vec<_> = std::thread::scope(|scope| {
                   let games: Vec<_> = batch
                       .iter()
                       .enumerate()
                       .map(|(place, seed)| {
                           let (setup, lowest_win) = (&setup, &lowest_win);
                           scope.spawn(move || {
                               let beaten = || lowest_win.load(Ordering::Relaxed) < place;
                               let game = play_unless(seed, setup, Human::Ai, &beaten);
                               if matches!(game, Some((_, ClaimedResult::Win, _))) {
                                   lowest_win.fetch_min(place, Ordering::Relaxed);
                               }
                               game
                           })
                       })
                       .collect();
                   games
                       .into_iter()
                       .map(|game| {
                           game.join()
                               .unwrap_or_else(|panic| std::panic::resume_unwind(panic))
                       })
                       .collect()
               });
               let won = batch.iter().zip(played).find_map(|(seed, game)| match game {
                   Some((log, ClaimedResult::Win, state)) => Some((seed, log, state)),
                   _ => None,
               });
               if let Some((seed, log, state)) = won {
                   return (seed.clone(), setup, log, state);
               }
           }
           panic!("the human wins none of {WIN_SEEDS} Easy games");
       })
   }
   ```
   Why the pick is unchanged:
   - A game is abandoned only when `lowest_win < place`, that is, when a lower seed has already won.
   - Any game at or below the final lowest winner never satisfies that, so it always runs to its end.
   - `find_map` over `batch.iter().zip(played)` returns the lowest place, which is what the old `find` returned.
   - If clippy's `type_complexity` fires on `Option<(Vec<Action>, ClaimedResult, GameState)>`, add `type Played = (Vec<Action>, ClaimedResult, GameState);` and use `Option<Played>`. Do not add an `#[allow]`.
4. Add a plain sync test right after `an_honest_win_pays_practice_rates` (see Tests). Name it so that it does not start with `r`, because names starting with `r` land in the other CI group.
5. Do not edit `scripts/ci-shards.toml`.

## Tests

In `crates/server/tests/api/practice.rs`:

```rust
#[test]
fn a_game_the_search_gives_up_on_stops_before_its_next_action() {
    jackioh_cards::register_all();
    let setup = setup(Difficulty::Easy, Vec::new());
    let asked = std::cell::Cell::new(0);
    let abandoned = || {
        asked.set(asked.get() + 1);
        asked.get() > 3
    };
    assert!(play_unless("practice-abandoned", &setup, Human::Ai, &abandoned).is_none());
    assert_eq!(asked.get(), 4, "asked before each action, and not again once it said yes");
}
```

- This asserts that `play_unless` returns `None` when told to stop, and that it asks exactly once before each action.
- It would fail on today's code, which has no `play_unless`.
- The existing six `honest_win` users and the `play(...)` tests keep proving the unchanged path.
- `play` still returns a finished game, because the wrapper's closure never abandons.

Commands, in order. The first build is cold and takes about 4 minutes:
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `time cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server -- api::practice::r`. Before: 27 passed, "finished in 154 s". After: all pass and the test run is **well under 30 s**; I expect about 5–10 s.
- `time cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server -- api::practice:: --skip api::practice::r`. All pass, also fast.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server -- a_game_the_search_gives_up_on`
- `cargo jackioh spec check`
